title: "switch() silently returns NULL when no case matches"
ref: FLW-05
categories: [Control flow]

extrait: 'is.null(switch("z", a = 1, b = 2))'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "an error, since `\"medium\"` is not handled"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
choice <- "medium"
size <- switch(choice, small = 1, large = 3)
size

switch(2, "a", "b")
switch(3, "a", "b")
```
:::

## Why

When no name matches and there is no default value, `switch()` returns `NULL`, and invisibly: nothing is printed. So `size` is `NULL`, and the error will surface further down, in a computation that has nothing to do with `switch()`.

With a number, `switch()` picks by position: `switch(2, "a", "b")` gives `"b"`, and `switch(3, "a", "b")` returns the same invisible `NULL`. With the string `"2"`, the unnamed cases become defaults, and R refuses to have two of them: `switch("2", "a", "b")` is a "duplicate 'switch' defaults" error.

## The remedy

End with an unnamed case that stops the program with a clear message.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
size <- switch(
  choice,
  small = 1,
  large = 3,
  stop("unknown choice: ", choice)
)
```
:::
